title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
LEFT HALF. This is a computation in the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex of the affine line, Omega_Gamma = k<T> ⊗ Λ(dT), with k<T> spanned by the T^{(i)}. It is the basic building block of the cosimplicial PD algebra C^·(Δ^n_*) used on the previous page. There Grothendieck writes F_*(X_*) = Hom(C^·(X_*), C^·(Δ^*_*)), a PD/integral analogue of the Sullivan realisation adjunction. On this page he names a family of operators on Omega_Gamma:
- d: the PD de Rham differential, with dT^{(i)} = T^{(i-1)}dT.
- λ: wedge multiplication by dT (written T̄∧).
- δ: the odd derivation that contracts with the Euler field, δ(dT) = T, δ(T^{(i)}) = 0.
- μ_i: multiplication by T^{(i)}; more generally μ_f is multiplication by any f in k<T>.
- θ: the weight (Euler) operator, θ(x) = deg x · x, where T and dT both have weight 1.

He lists the (super)commutation relations:
- d^2 = δ^2 = λ^2 = 0.
- dλ + λd = 0.
- dδ + δd = θ (Cartan's formula: the Lie derivative along the Euler field is the weight).
- δλ + λδ = μ_1 = μ_T.
- dμ_f − μ_f d = μ_{f'}λ, i.e. dμ_i − μ_i d = μ_{i−1}λ.
- [λ, μ_i] = [δ, μ_i] = 0.
- [d, θ] = [δ, θ] = 0.
- [θ, λ] = λ.
- [θ, μ_f] = μ_{θf}, i.e. [θ, μ_i] = iμ_i.
- μ_f μ_g = μ_{fg}, i.e. μ_i μ_j = binom(i+j, i) μ_{i+j}.

He then seeks a PBW-type normal form for the algebra these operators generate: Σ f_{αβσn} λ^α d^β δ^σ θ^n with α, β, σ in F_2 and n in N. He begins computing products of two normal-form monomials, using reordering terms such as g α θ + β g' λ.

The purpose is to understand homotopies and the Poincaré lemma for PD de Rham complexes, uniformly in the characteristic. Note θ is not invertible in characteristic p, so the homotopy δ alone does not contract. A side check verifies a toy operator φ with φλ − λφ = λ.

RIGHT HALF. He builds the PD de Rham (Koszul-type) complex DR^{Γ,q}_* = Γ^pΦ_* ⊗ Λ^qΨ_* attached to a linear map s: Φ → Ψ of (simplicial) modules. The differential on generators is d(φ^{(p)}) = s(φ) φ^{(p−1)}. To check this is well defined on Γ^p, which is not generated by p-th powers, he treats (φ, ψ) ↦ s(φ⊗ψ)φ^{(p−1)} as a polynomial law. He expands f(Σλ_iφ_i) and extracts the coefficient of λ_1^{q_1}…λ_r^{q_r}. This yields the explicit formula
 d(φ_1^{(q_1)}…φ_r^{(q_r)}) = Σ_{α: q_α ≥ 1} s(φ_α) φ_1^{(q_1)}…φ_α^{(q_α−1)}…φ_r^{(q_r)},
the comultiplication Γ^q → Γ^{q−1} ⊗ Γ^1 followed by s.

He compares this with the composite Γ^q → Γ^{q−1}⊗Φ → Γ^q (multiplication back), which gives Σ q_α ψ φ^{(q)}, i.e. multiplication by the degree. This is again an Euler-type identity, now for the Koszul complex Γ⊗Λ. There is also a tentative exact sequence relating Γ^p of an extension Φ_1 → Φ → Φ_2 to Γ^pΦ⊗Φ and Γ^pΦ⊗Ψ, with question marks, and a factorisation question (Γ^2Φ ⊗ Φ vs Γ^2Φ ⊗ Ψ). At the bottom he records the naming: DR_*^{Γ,q} = Γ^pΦ_* ⊗ Λ^qΨ_*, and ΛΦ_* = C_*^{Γ,0}.
errors: The transcription line 'φλ − λφ = λx' should read φλ − λφ = λ (the stray x is an evaluation slip).
'δ(T) = T' in the boxed list conflicts with δ(T^{(i)}) = 0. The consistent reading is δ(dT) = T, δ(T) = 0; the Euler-derivation interpretation requires this.
The exact sequence 0 → Γ^pΦ_1 → Γ^pΦ⊗Φ → Γ^pΦ_2⊗Ψ → 0 is written tentatively. As transcribed it is not exact in general (ranks do not match); Grothendieck himself marks it with '?'.
'θ^2 = …' is left unfinished: no relation for θ^2 is needed, since θ generates a polynomial subalgebra.

ideas.what: Operator (super)algebra on the PD de Rham complex of A^1 generated by d, wedge with dT, Euler contraction δ, multiplications μ_f and the weight θ, with Cartan relations and a PBW normal form
ideas.modern_name: Cartan calculus / PD Weyl-type differential operator superalgebra; Euler homotopy dδ+δd = weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan (Cartan formula); PD de Rham Poincaré lemma: Berthelot, Illusie (1970s)
ideas.where_published: 1976 IHES lecture on the PD de Rham complex, unpublished

ideas.what: Differential on Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^qΨ for s: Φ→Ψ, defined via polynomial laws, with explicit formula on products of divided powers; Euler identity for the composite
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complex Γ⊗Λ / divided-power de Rham–Koszul complex of a linear map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, ch. I §4), Roby (polynomial laws), Quillen

ideas.what: Use of cosimplicial PD de Rham algebras C^·(Δ^n) as a PD/integral analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms (context from the previous page)
ideas.modern_name: integral/PD models of simplicial sets via divided-power polynomial forms

missed.claim: Grothendieck worked out an explicit normal form Σ f λ^α d^β δ^σ θ^n for the operator algebra acting on the PD de Rham complex of the line, as a tool for a characteristic-free Poincaré lemma for PD forms on simplices. This is a documented, but standard-level, detail of the unpublished 1976 IHES lecture.
missed.quote: Σ μ_{f_{αβσ}} λ^α d^β δ^σ θ^n  α,β,σ ∈ F_2, n ∈ N
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's parallel to Cartan's 1976 PD cochain algebras and to later integral models of homotopy types. The mathematics itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct, standard computations: Cartan-type relations and Koszul/PD de Rham differentials via polynomial laws. Historically they are mildly interesting as part of an unpublished lecture on PD de Rham forms on simplices, but nothing on the page is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'δ(T) = T' should likely be δ(dT) = T (or δ(T̄) = T, with T̄ denoting dT).
'φλ − λφ = λx' should be φλ − λφ = λ.
λ is written 'T̄∧', i.e. wedge with dT (T̄ = dT), not a conjugate.
The struck-out line at the top left is Λ^iΦ ⊗ ΛΨ (deleted).
The right-hand header reads roughly '(car p quelconque ≥ 2), q = 1'. The sequence below it probably involves Γ^pΦ_1 → Γ^pΦ_*⊗Φ_* → Γ^pΦ_2⊗Ψ_*, but the subscripts are uncertain.
